column1: # cac group, build A (note 0009 D7.1, B06). Builder A, 2026-11-20.
# Sources: EasyMesh through the usp-spec MCP server (doc easymesh): §3.1.2 Conventions (bit/byte order per [2] = IEEE
#   1905.1, multi-octet integers big-endian; reserved objects set to zero by the sender, ignored by the recipient),
#   TLV codes from the tables match em-types codes.rs:306-308 (0xad-0xaf), 310 (0xb1), 347-351 (0xd6-0xda) and
#   Upstream (pinned ba4180b, read from an extracted copy): em_channel.cpp:1367-1464 (0xb1 sender: three count+list
#   sections, htons Minutes/Duration, 3-octet Countdown most significant first at :1449-1451), :1466-1507 (0xaf sender:
#   one group per local radio, op class/channel/status/pairs copied from one global record; Num_Radio 0 when the data
#   model has no radios), callers :1559-1574; :944-968 (0xd8) and :1166-1194 (0xd9) senders with no caller;
#   :1649-1663 (0xe8/0xe9: 8 uninitialised octets, no JSON). No upstream sender for 0xad, 0xae, 0xd6, 0xd7, 0xda.
#   Every port_rule is SPEC (line 160: "-", no difference). Note 0009 D2 (raw reserved values, zero counts), D4, D5
#   (JSON objects are raw octets), D8; 0008 D4 (0xb1 3-octet countdown). No table in this group says "one or more",
#   so every zero count here is a spec case.
# Wire layouts (hex = tlvValue only; multi-octet integers big-endian per §3.1.2):
#   0xad: Num_Radio(1), Num_Radio x { RUID(6), OpClass(1), Channel(1), octet: CAC Method b7-5, CAC Completion Action
#         b4-3, Reserved b2-0 }. Method 4-7 and Action 2-3 are reserved values, carried raw (D2). (The table lists
#         "011" both as Time sliced CAC and in the reserved range "011"-"111"; 3 is read as Time sliced.)
#   0xae: Num_Radio(1), Num_Radio x { RUID(6), OpClass(1), Channel(1) }.
#   0xaf: Num_Radio(1), Num_Radio x { RUID(6), OpClass(1), Channel(1), CAC Completion Status(1; 0x06-0xff reserved,
#         raw), Num_Pair(1), Num_Pair x { OpClass(1), Channel(1) } }. Num_Pair has no cap (audit 158; upstream caps 4).
#   0xb1: Num_Available(1), n x { OpClassA(1), ChannelA(1), Minutes(2, BE) }, Num_PairNon(1), n x { OpClassN(1),
#         ChannelN(1), Duration(2, BE) }, Num_PairActive(1), n x { OpClassC(1), ChannelC(1), Countdown(3, BE) }.
#         All three counts may be 0: minimum value 3 octets (audit 162).
#   0xd6: Num_OpClass(1), Num_OpClass x { OpClass(1), Num_Chan(1), Num_Chan x Channel(1), Reserved(4) }. Counts may be
#   0xd7: OpClass(1), Channel(1), Reference BSSID(6), Num_Usage(1), Num_Usage x { Burst Start Time(4, BE), Burst
#         Length(4, BE), Repetitions(4, BE), Burst Interval(4, BE), RU Bitmask Length(1), RU Bitmask(RU Bitmask Length
#         octets, raw), Transmitter identifier(6), Power Level(1, signed; 0xff = unknown), Channel Usage Reason(1;
#         5-254 reserved, raw; 255 = BSS non-usage), Reserved(4) }. Num_Usage may be 0 (9 octets, audit 264).
#   0xd8: RUID(6), octet: Reserved b7-6, BSS Color b5-0; octet: Reserved b7-5, HESIGA_Spatial_reuse_value15_allowed b4,
#         SRG Information Valid b3, Non-SRG Offset Valid b2, Reserved b1, PSR Disallowed b0; Non-SRG OBSSPD Max
#         Offset(1), SRG OBSSPD Min Offset(1), SRG OBSSPD Max Offset(1), SRG BSS Color Bitmap(8, raw), SRG Partial
#         BSSID Bitmap(8, raw), Reserved(2). Exactly 29 octets. Offsets and bitmaps are always present and carried as
#         found whatever the valid flags say.
#   0xd9: RUID(6), octet: Reserved b7, Partial BSS Color b6, BSS Color b5-0; flags octet as 0xd8; the three offsets,
#         SRG BSS Color Bitmap(8), SRG Partial BSSID Bitmap(8), NeighborBSSColorInUseBitmap(8), Reserved(2). Exactly 37.
#   0xe8 / 0xe9: the whole value is one JSON object, carried as raw octets (D5); no length prefix, not parsed.
#   (1) Items are written in the listed order. Widths: ruid, rN_ruid, ref_bssid, uK_tx_id are 6-octet MACs (12 hex
#       digits). aK_minutes, nK_duration, tail_reserved: 2 octets BE. cK_countdown: 3 octets BE. uK_start, uK_length,
#       uK_reps, uK_interval, uK_reserved, oK_reserved: 4 octets BE. uK_power: signed decimal written as one 2's
#       complement octet (-1 = 0xff, the "unknown" value). Every other integer item is 1 octet. Values are decimal or
#   (2) Byte-string items srg_color_bitmap, srg_bssid_bitmap, neighbor_bitmap, uK_ru and json are hex: raw octets,
#       written exactly as given with NO length octet in front (uK_ru's length is the separate uK_ru_len item).
#   (3) Count items (radios, rN_pairs, avail, nonocc, active, opclasses, oK_chans, usages) and length items (uK_ru_len)
#       are written as given; only the entries listed follow (a count or length above the listed data = overstated).
#       Entry names: 0xad/0xae/0xaf rN_*, 0xaf pairs rN_pK_class/rN_pK_ch; 0xb1 aK_* (available), nK_* (non-occupancy),
#       cK_* (active CAC); 0xd6 oK_class, oK_chans, oK_chJ, oK_reserved; 0xd7 uK_*.
#   (4) Reserved octet items (oK_reserved, uK_reserved: 4 octets; tail_reserved: 2 octets) are integers like any other
#       item, listed explicitly in every complete entry (0 = zero octets) and written at their own position. A row in
#       which one is not listed has no octets for it (a cut entry, rule 6).
#   (5) Bit-field octets: each group below is ONE octet, written at the position of the group's first listed item;
#       values are unshifted; a reserved mask is given in octet position and ORed in (absent = 0):
#       0xad {rN_method b7-5, rN_action b4-3, rN_reserved b2-0}; 0xd8 {color_reserved b7-6, bss_color b5-0} and
#       {hesiga15 b4, srg_valid b3, non_srg_valid b2, psr_disallowed b0, flags_reserved b7-5,b1}; 0xd9 {color_reserved
#       b7, partial_color b6, bss_color b5-0} and the same flags group. A case that sets a reserved mask or reserved
#       octets: the decoder ignores them; the encoder writes zero (canonical bytes = the *-clear sibling / same fields
#   (6) An item given as hex: where it normally takes a MAC or integer is a cut field: exactly those raw octets are
#       written (hex: alone = nothing written). An item not listed is absent from the bytes.
#   (7) trailing=hex: raw octets appended after the listed fields.
# Choices (for the coordinator): (a) every cut field, partial entry or overstated count/length is error=Truncated (as
#   B01-B05); extra octets after a complete layout are TrailingBytes. (b) Zero Num_Radio in 0xad, 0xae and 0xaf is
#   kind=spec (no "one or more" in Tables 64-66; same reading as B05). (c) 0xaf success-with-pairs (status 0x00,
#   Num_Pair 1) and radar-no-pairs (status 0x01, Num_Pair 0) are kind=spec: well-formed bytes, the "shall be set to
#   zero if radar was not detected" rule is a value rule for the consumer (not the 0xa6 omitted-fields precedent).
#   (d) 0xd7 ru-len-4-unlisted (RU Bitmask Length 4 with 4 octets) is kind=spec: the length describes the bytes (D2);
#   conflicting precedent: D3 line 222 rejected unlisted MCS NSS lengths as InvalidLength. (e) 0xd7
#   interval-without-reps (Repetitions 0, Burst Interval non-zero; "set to zero if Repetitions field is zero") is
#   kind=spec, a value rule for the consumer. (f) 0xe8/0xe9: the codec does not parse JSON (D5), so non-JSON octets
#   (upstream's 8 uninitialised octets are of this kind) are kind=spec; the empty value is kind=invalid;error=Truncated
#   because the table requires one JSON object. (g) 0xd8/0xd9 bitmaps and offsets are carried when the valid flags
#   are 0 (kind=spec). (h) 0xb1 counts above 255 cannot be written; the encoder's CountTooLarge (0008 D4) has no
#   fixture row. (i) The 0xad Method value 3 typo is read as Time sliced CAC; the codec carries the raw value anyway.
